I know it has not that much to do with the article itself but i was wondering who the General Secretary of Public Revenue was. This is the result of the short research.

Being Secretary General of Public Revenue in greece is not an easy job. Haris Theoharis, who had the position before her resigned in 2014 after receiving death threats and political pressure. He was appointed through a public offering in february 2013 and was trying to get foreign Greek bondholders to pay taxes for their titles and overall trying to crack down on the country’s endemic tax evasion. Not an easy job.

  • "The term of the General Secretary of Public Revenue has a length of five years, is an independent non-political appointment, and the only possibility for Theoharis to be removed from his position is only by tendering his resignation."

Given that Theoharis said, “The government took decisions, not me,” it's understandable that he quit.

But it must be noted that:

  • the position of general secretary was was created in 2012 under pressure from Greece’s troika of international creditors with a view to making the country’s tax administration more independent. More info about that can be found in the 2012 Memorandum of Economic and Financial Policies (MEFP)

The new general secretary Aikaterini Savvaidou, appointed in June 2014 by Antonis Samaris (former greek prime minister). So much for the independent non-political appointment of this position... I can't really find anything on how she was really appointed. Not to say that Varoufakis is right in that she is being controlled by the Troika, but being appointed (or whatever) by the Prime minister, or being proposed by Gikas Hardouvelis (then finance minister) is the opposite of non-political. She also seems far from being "clean".

Before she became general secretary she worked for PwC as Tax senior Manager. PwC, which does auditing, tax consulting and corporate consulting "one of the so-called Big Four accounting firms of the world". Apparently so good, that they "have helped hundreds of clients cut their corporation tax bills by setting up bases in Luxembourg." But they (PwC) seem like very nice people they even said:

  • "We agree the tax system is too complex, as governments compete for investment and tax revenues."
  • "We take our responsibility to build trust in the tax system seriously and will continue to support reform."

"in the LuxLeaks case, PwC is the real protagonist. The company set up tax avoidance schemes, in collusion with Luxembourg authorities, for more than 340 multinationals. Among them are at least 9 companies associated with Greece."

So, appointing a person that was an active manager at the firm when all those tax evasion schemes were at work does not seem so wise. Conflict of interest anyone??

And she was apparently proposed by Gikas Hardouvelis, as head of a five member committee, to be appointed General Secretary of Public Revenues. Followed by a final decision of the cabinet. See here

If you want to know what Varoufakis said in the recorded call and what his Plan B - in case of the banks shutting down - was, just read this:

“What we planned to do was the following. There is the website of the tax office like there is in Britain and everywhere else, where citizens, taxpayers go into the website they use their tax file number and they transfer through web banking monies from the bank account to their tax file number so as to make payments on VAT, income tax and so on and so forth.”

“We were planning to create, surreptitiously, reserve accounts attached to every tax file number, without telling anyone, just to have this system in a function under wraps. And, at the touch of a button, to allow us to give PIN numbers to tax file number holders, to taxpayers. So let’s take for instance the case the state owed 1 million euros to some pharmaceutical company for drugs purchased on behalf of the National Health Service. We could immediately create a digital transfer into that reserve account of the tax file number of the pharmaceutical company and provide them with a pin number so that they could use this as a kind of parallel payment mechanism by whichever part of that digital monies to any tax file number for whom they owed money or indeed to use it to in order to make tax payments to the state. That would have created a parallel banking system while the banks were shut as a result of the ECBs aggressive action to deny us some breathing space.”
